summary: Attention to Detail's Rollcage games and GRIP: Combat Racing, the later spiritual successor by Caged Element, all centered on ultra-fast double-sided vehicles that can drive on walls and ceilings while using combat powerups.

entries.title: Rollcage
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release with Redux compatibility build where available

emulation.notes: Use the PC release for the main route; emulate PlayStation only for console preservation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC release with modern compatibility fixes

primary.version: PC release with modern Redux compatibility build where available
primary.why: Rollcage released on Windows and PlayStation. Windows is the highest-fidelity route for the 3D-accelerated wall-and-ceiling combat racer, and a later unofficial Rollcage Redux build fixes bugs and supports newer hardware.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version on original-compatible hardware or with the Rollcage Redux compatibility build if using original game files; use PlayStation as the console alternative.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with 3D accelerator support and modern Redux compatibility option.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most practical modern route.
skip: console route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced PlayStation-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Rollcage Redux is an unofficial compatibility update, not a commercial remaster.

entries.title: Rollcage Stage II / Death Track Racing
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release / Death Track Racing with compatibility build where available

emulation.notes: Use the PC release for main fidelity and PlayStation emulation only for console preservation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC release with compatibility fixes

primary.version: PC release / Death Track Racing with modern Extreme compatibility build where available
primary.why: Rollcage Stage II released on PlayStation and Windows, with the North American Windows release repackaged as Death Track Racing. The Windows version supports the strongest fidelity path, including hardware-accelerated bump mapping on supported hardware and the later unofficial Rollcage Extreme compatibility build.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version with modern compatibility fixes where available; use PlayStation only for console preservation.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release, also sold as Death Track Racing in North America, with hardware-accelerated bump mapping support and later compatibility builds.

all_releases.reason: skip: console route and no sourced content advantage over Windows.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced PlayStation-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Rollcage Extreme is an unofficial compatibility update, not a commercial remaster.
